objective: Implement a deterministic economic-calendar/event schema with explicit scheduled versus actual release timing, IANA timezone semantics, lifecycle invariants and P10-A source provenance without introducing release values, revisions or surprise calculations.
scope: Define canonical economic-event categories and lifecycle statuses
Bind each event to a canonical P10-A official source
Preserve source-scoped event identity, jurisdiction and reference period
Preserve scheduled release time and declared IANA timezone
Preserve actual release time only for RELEASED state
Preserve rescheduled-from time only for RESCHEDULED state
Preserve cancellation reason only for CANCELLED state
Preserve calendar observed-at time and trusted dataset/quality provenance
Enforce point-in-time lifecycle invariants fail closed
out_of_scope: Actual, forecast or previous numeric values
Signal probability, Risk approval or execution
dependencies: Fresh Live Guard: open PRs 0, active task none, active lock none
tests: Strict Pyright passes for P10 economic-event source/tests
Event source must exist in P10-A official-source registry
SCHEDULED events cannot carry release/reschedule/cancellation fields
RELEASED events require actual_release_time_ns not after observed_at_ns
Dataset version and quality evidence require SHA-256
Event identity is deterministic and content-sensitive
Event schema contains no actual/forecast/previous values or trading authority
P10-B evidence is byte-identical across two runs
rollback: Revert P10-B event schema/policy/tests/evidence/CI wiring and state reconciliation. P10-A remains canonical and no production/trading state changes.
definition_of_done: Deterministic evidence and strict CI pass
Post-merge Governance and Branch Hygiene pass
